ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Act on Reporting and Use of Certain Financial Transaction Information (Korea AML/CFT Act) (Act No. 6516, September 3, 2001, as amended); Presidential Enforcement Decree on the Reporting and Use of Certain Financial Transaction Information; Financial Services Commission Regulation on Identification and Verification of Customers and Beneficial Ownership; Act on Prohibition of Financing of Terrorism and Proliferation of Weapons of Mass Destruction (Act No. 9527, March 31, 2009, as amended); and Supreme Court Registry Regulations implementing the Commercial Act on corporate formation.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the Ultimate Beneficial Owner and any immediate parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies Registry / Corporate Registry in the foreign jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: (1) notarize the certificate before the competent notary in the issuing country; (2) obtain a paper or e-Apostille from the Designated Competent Authority of that country under the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention; (3) present the notarized, apostilled original to the Korean FIU and corporate registry without further legalization. Non-member consular path: (1) notarize at the issuing country's notary; (2) authenticate the notarized original at the issuing country's Ministry of Foreign Affairs; (3) legalize it at the Embassy or Consulate of the Republic of Korea with jurisdiction over the issuing country; (4) never apply both an Apostille and consular legalization to the same instrument.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Certificate of Active Status) of the founding/UBO entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies Registry or Registrar of Corporations in the UBO jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: If the issuing state is an Apostille Member, the certificate must be notarized and then apostilled by the issuing state's Competent Authority and forwarded directly; if the issuing state is not an Apostille Member, the notarized certificate must be authenticated by the foreign ministry and legalized by the Korean Consulate. The two routes are mutually exclusive.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Original Board Resolution / Power of Attorney authorizing the formation of KR Yuhan Hoesa and appointment of registered directors and corporate representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the parent company, attested by the corporate secretary or notary public in the UBO jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarize the signature of the board chairperson and corporate secretary, then obtain a Hague Apostille from the issuing jurisdiction's Competent Authority if the jurisdiction is an Apostille Member; for non-member states, execute consular legalization at the Korean Embassy/Consulate after foreign ministry authentication. Do not combine the Apostille with consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association / Memorandum of Incorporation of the parent entity, plus the draft Korean-language Articles of Association of KR Yuhan Hoesa
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign corporate registry for the parent instruments; Korean licensed law firm for the draft Articles of Association
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parent Articles must follow the relevant apostille or consular legalization route depending on the issuer's membership in the Apostille Convention; the draft Korean Articles are notarized before a Korean notary and recorded in the Korean Commercial Registry, requiring no foreign legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter for the UBO/contributing entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed commercial bank in the UBO's jurisdiction that maintains the operating account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The bank letter must be signed by an authorized bank officer and notarized; thereafter, if the bank's home country is an Apostille Member, obtain an Apostille from the country's Competent Authority; if the country is not a member, have the letter authenticated by the country's foreign ministry and then legalized by the Korean Consulate. Never chain both methods.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Every UBO, shareholder owning directly or indirectly 25% or more, director, officer, and authorized signatory must be screened prior to formation against (i) the Korean Financial Intelligence Unit's PEP and Watch-List indications under the AML/CFT Act, (ii) OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists, (iii) the United Nations Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List, (iv) the EU consolidated financial sanctions list, and (v) Korean domestic unilateral sanctions and anti-terrorism designations. The screening must include adverse media, litigation, bankruptcy, and regulatory enforcement checks, and the completed PEP declaration and risk score must be preserved for not less than five years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Registry Information System / Internet Registration Office (IROS)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Korean Commercial Act Article 17 requires a corporate name to be in Hangul and to end with 'Yuhan Hoesa' (or the approved legal form suffix). Foreign-language names must be transliterated phonetically into Hangul or translated into Korean, with the official Chinese-character (Hanja) spelling, if any, shown in parentheses. The four-tier naming convention is (1) a distinctive Hangul brand element; (2) a business-object clause matching the ISIC 1074 / NAICS 311412 description, e.g., 'steamed dumpling and dim sum quick-freezing manufacturing'; (3) the legal-form suffix 'Yuhan Hoesa'; and (4) a registered head-office administrative district term used by the tax registry. The corporate name must be identical in the business registration certificate.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: South Korea Commercial Act (Act No. 1000, as most recently amended), Chapter III, Section 5 on Yuhan Hoesa (limited liability companies), Articles 287 through 287-26, together with the Commercial Registration Act and the Regulations on Commercial Registration issued by the Supreme Court of Korea
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Registry Division of the District Court having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office of the Company, administered under the Court Administration of the Supreme Court of Korea, with electronic filing through the Court E-Registry (E-reg) portal
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Yuhan Hoesa (beop-in deung-gi sincheongseo), accompanied by the notarized Articles of Incorporation, capital verification certificate, office consent documents, and statutory officer acceptance forms prescribed by the Commercial Registration Act
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is imposed on a Yuhan Hoesa under Korean law. The subscribers must fully pay or provide the aggregate contributed capital amount stated in the Articles of Incorporation before the incorporation registration date. The paid-in contribution must be deposited into a corporate subscription bank account opened in the Company's name, and a bank balance verification certificate must accompany the registration filing. There is no statutory blocked-escrow account requirement beyond this payment obligation. Capital may be paid in cash or in-kind; in-kind contributions must be valued by an independent accredited appraiser, and non-resident capital remittances must be declared and processed under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION OF YUHANG HOESA (THE COMPANY) - ADOPTED UNANIMOUSLY ON [DATE] AT THE COMPANY'S PRINCIPAL OFFICE. WHEREAS, the Company is being incorporated as a Yuhan Hoesa under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea; and WHEREAS, the subscribers have executed the Company's Articles of Incorporation, established the initial statutory capital, and nominated the statutory officers; and WHEREAS, the Company intends to engage in the industrial quick-freezing of steamed dim sum and dumplings under ISIC 1074, and will obtain all necessary food, environmental, and fire licenses; NOW, THEREFORE, IT IS HEREBY RESOLVED: 1. CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION: That the aggregate initial contributed capital of KRW [AMOUNT] be, and it is, approved and recorded in the Company's capital account; the subscription schedule is ratified; all contributions are to be paid to a bank subscription account in the Company's name before the incorporation registration application is filed. 2. BANKING AUTHORIZATION: That [Representative Director Name], [Additional Director Name], and [Compliance Officer Name] be, and they are, jointly and severally authorized to open operating, foreign-currency, and utility accounts at any authorized commercial bank in the Republic of Korea; each bank contract and electronic banking mandate is approved; any payment instrument exceeding KRW [AMOUNT] must bear the signature of the representative director and one additional authorized officer. 3. REGISTERED OFFICE: That the registered office of the Company is adopted as [Address, District, City, Republic of Korea]; the representative director is authorized to execute leases, obtain landlord consent certificates, and file address changes with the Commercial Registry. 4. STATUTORY OFFICERS: That [Name] is appointed as Representative Director and Chief Executive Officer; [Name] is appointed as Director; and [Name] is appointed as Auditor, unless lawfully exempted under the Articles of Incorporation; each officer shall have the powers and duties granted by the Commercial Act and the Articles of Incorporation. 5. INCORPORATION AND LICENSING ACTIONS: That legal counsel and the officers are authorized to sign all applications to the District Court Commercial Registry, National Tax Service, Ministry of Food and Drug Safety, local government food sanitation office, fire department, and environmental authority; all necessary consents, verifications, permits, and certificates shall be filed within applicable statutory deadlines. 6. GENERAL PROVISIONS: That this resolution is effective upon adoption and remains in full force and effect until amended or rescinded; the minutes of this meeting shall be maintained at the registered office and certified copies shall be delivered to the registry, banks, and licensing authorities as required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Reservation, Business Scope Confirmation, and Notarized Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: District Court Commercial Registry of the intended registered office, using the Court E-Registry portal, together with a licensed Korean notary public
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name availability search for the Korean corporate name and confirm the business purpose within ISIC 1074 and Korean Standard Industrial Classification. Prepare Articles of Incorporation in Korean, stipulating the corporate name, purpose, registered office address, aggregate contributed capital, number of contributed investment units, method of contribution, appointment of representative director, term of officers, accounting period, and meeting provisions. All subscribers must execute the articles and provide certified copies of identity documents; non-resident subscribers must execute the articles before a notary public or through a lawfully appointed power of attorney. Have the Articles notarized by a Korean notary public, submit the executed notarized articles to the District Court registration counsel for conformity review, and arrange the applicable registration tax and court fee stamps as directed.
required_dossiers: Proposed Korean corporate name in Hangeul with English transliteration
Passport and resident registration certificate or corporate certificate of each subscriber
Power of attorney if execution is made by proxy
Consent to use of registered office address or lease agreement
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Statement of business purpose under ISIC 1074
Foreign Exchange Transactions Act declaration plan for non-resident subscribers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name reservation is rejected, file a modified name reservation and respond to the registry objection; if notarization or subscriber execution is queried, cure by re-executing the Articles and obtaining a supplementary notarial certificate before the incorporation filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Subscription Payment and Bank Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Authorized foreign exchange commercial bank in Korea; responsible financial institution under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary corporate subscription bank account at an authorized foreign exchange commercial bank within the territorial district of the registered office. Issue a collection instruction showing the beneficiary account and subscriber particulars; each cash contribution may be paid by same-day wire if declared under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act for non-resident investors, or by ordinary transfer for resident subscribers. After the final contribution date, request the bank to issue a balance verification certificate showing the total paid-in capital and the deposit date. For in-kind contributions, prepare a contribution-in-kind report and obtain an independent valuation report from an accredited appraiser. Record the capital receipts in the Company's pre-registration capital ledger and retain bank remittance confirmations and foreign-exchange transaction certificates for submission with the registration filing.
required_dossiers: Subscription and capital payment schedule
Bank remittance slips and foreign exchange transaction certificates
Passport or corporate proof of each subscriber
Bank balance verification certificate for paid-in capital
In-kind contribution appraisal report, if applicable
Completed foreign exchange declaration receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank queries the source of funds, provide certified true copies of identity, business purpose, and wealth evidence; if funds are held for foreign exchange declaration defects, correct the declaration and resubmit before capital verification can be completed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Meeting and Adoption of the First Board Resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company principal office, notary public office, and the statutory officers of the Company
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene at the Company's registered office or any properly noticed place. For each subscriber, confirm presence and voting rights; for the directors, confirm statutory quorum pursuant to the Articles of Incorporation. Distribute the agenda, present the Articles of Incorporation, the capital subscription schedule, and the officer candidates, then propose the first formal resolution. The chair shall call the resolution; all subscribers and directors present shall vote; minutes must be written in Korean with an English translation, signed by the chair, countersigned by the secretary, and stamped by each director or member. The minutes should authorize the opening of the corporate operating account, appointment of the representative director and auditor, adoption of the registered office, and authority to execute all incorporation documents. If notarization is required by the registry, the minutes shall be notarized before filing.
required_dossiers: Notice or waiver of meeting
Attendance register and capital account register
First Board Resolution minutes signed by chair and secretary
Officer appointment acceptance forms
Passport or ID copies of appointed officers
Statutory auditor consent form, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a minute defect or notarization defect is alleged, execute a curative second shareholder and director resolution ratifying all first-meeting acts before submitting the incorporation registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Incorporation Registration Filing with the Commercial Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registry Division, District Court having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office, through the Court E-Registry (E-reg)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the prescribed Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Yuhan Hoesa with the Commercial Registry of the District Court having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office. Attach the statutory dossier set and submit electronically using the court e-registry. Pay the court fee and registration tax through the court payment system. The registrar will review legal compliance, verify whether the directors and auditor accept office, check capital verification, and compare the registered office consent with the building ledger. If satisfied, the registrar enters the Company into the commercial register and issues a Certificate of Registered Matters, corporate seal certificate, and registration number. The representative director must receive the certificate, check all registered details, and deliver the official certified copy to the Company's statutory records binder.
required_dossiers: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Yuhan Hoesa
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Original meeting minutes incorporating the First Board Resolution
Bank balance certificate evidencing paid-in capital
Lease agreement or landlord consent for registered office
Certified copies of directors and auditor identification
Power of attorney executed in favor of counsel
Receipt of payment of registration tax and court fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a correction order or query, prepare supplementary explanations and amended documents within ten days; if the registrar rejects the application, rectify the stated omissions, re-file the application, and where necessary appeal the registrar's administrative decision through the competent appellate procedure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Registration and Food Manufacturing License Submission
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local District Tax Office under the National Tax Service, and the local district or county food and health administrative authority, together with the Ministry of Food and Drug Safety regional office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After incorporation registration, file the beginning-of-business registration with the local District Tax Office within the statutory period, stating the industrial interest in the manufacture of frozen dumplings and dim sum and listing the factory location. Then submit the Food Manufacturing and Processing Business License application under Article 36 of the Food Sanitation Act to the competent local food and health authority or the local Ministry of Food and Drug Safety office. The application must include the factory blueprints, food handling and quick-freeze processing equipment descriptions, cold and frozen storage plans, wastewater treatment plan, environmental impact consultation documents if triggered, and fire safety certification. The authority will inspect the premises, review HACCP-based sanitation plans, and issue the license upon approval; foreign-invested companies should present the foreign direct investment registration certificate if capital has been remitted.
required_dossiers: Certificate of registered matters issued by the Commercial Registry
Corporate seal certificate and corporate ID information
Application for Food Manufacturing and Processing Business License
Factory and equipment layout drawings
Cold storage and quick-freezing facility specifications
Water supply and sewage discharge treatment plans
HACCP or food safety management plan
Waste management contract with licensed waste handler
Fire-fighting systems completion certificate and inspection report
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the food authority issues a supplementary request, correct the facility deficiencies and submit revised blueprints and inspection reports; if the license is refused, exhaust administrative appeal with the competent authority and, if necessary, initiate judicial review while maintaining the business registration as a legally dormant manufacturing plan.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Food and Drug Safety (MFDS) regional office, local Gu/Si health and food sanitation department, Ministry of Environment through the local Environmental Management Office, and the local fire station under the National Fire Agency
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Food Manufacturing and Processing Business License under Article 36 of the Food Sanitation Act; for a physically operating prefabricated dim sum factory, a mandatory statutory manufacturing license is issued before the commencement of production

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment of the Republic of Korea, acting through the local Environmental Management Office and the municipal environmental department
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Small-Scale Environmental Impact Assessment is required where the factory site area exceeds 10,000 square meters; for a typical smaller frozen food factory, an Environmental Consultation or Registration under the Environmental Impact Assessment Act and a Wastewater Discharge Facility registration or permit under the Water Environment Conservation Act will be triggered; a Full Environmental Impact Assessment Report is required only if the factory project falls within the project categories and size thresholds for full EIA under the Enforcement Decree of the Environmental Impact Assessment Act.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Treated effluent for a food manufacturing wastewater discharge facility must generally meet these discharge limits to public waters: Biochemical Oxygen Demand (BOD) not exceeding 20 mg/L, Chemical Oxygen Demand (COD) not exceeding 40 mg/L, Suspended Solids (SS) not exceeding 20 mg/L, Total Nitrogen not exceeding 20 mg/L, Total Phosphorus not exceeding 0.6 mg/L, and pH within 5.8 to 8.6. Volatile organic compound (VOC) emitting equipment, including refrigeration condensers and any solvent-based cleaning stations, must comply with CleanAir Conservation Act stack concentration and fugitive emission standards. Hazardous waste, including used lubricants and refrigerant oils, must be stored in approved containers and transported and disposed of by licensed waste treatment businesses, with electronic manifests filed through the Korea Environmental Corporation waste management system.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Firefighting Systems Completion Certificate and final fire inspection approval must be obtained from the local fire station under the Fire-Fighting and Construction Act before production. The factory building must receive structural load inspection and approval for freezer floors, quick-freeze lines, mezzanine equipment platforms, and ammonia or Freon refrigeration machinery. Occupational Safety and Health Act clearance must be obtained through a workplace safety audit covering conveyor guarding, lockout-tagout procedures, cold-storage entry permits, pressure vessel certification, and electrical safety inspection by the Korea Electrical Safety Corporation before energization. Sanitary facility inspection by the food and health authority is required as a condition precedent to operating the dim sum production facility.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea, acting through the HomeTax electronic tax portal (www.hometax.go.kr); export customs validation is coordinated with the Korea Customs Service through UNI-PASS (portal.customs.go.kr).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For the Yuhan Hoesa (Korean LLC) owned by a foreign non-resident investor, the company must first complete incorporation under the Korean Commercial Act and then apply for Business Registration at the local NTS district tax office (or via HomeTax) within the statutory 20-day period from business commencement. Required documents include the Certificate of Corporate Seal, Articles of Incorporation, Certificate of Incorporation, place-of-business lease or property documentation, foreign investment report or certificate if received under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, and passport or government-issued ID of the representative director. NTS will issue a Business Registration Certificate containing the 10-digit Business Registration Number (BRN), which is the unified Korean TIN and VAT registration number for corporate duties. The company must then activate electronic tax invoice issuance on HomeTax. If the foreign non-resident parent has Korean-source income but no domestic permanent establishment, the parent must appoint a statutory tax representative and register for a non-resident tax identification file with the competent NTS International Taxation Office for withholding tax and treaty reduction purposes. No separate VAT ID is required for the domestic LLC beyond the BRN.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. The Korean Corporate Tax Act and VAT Act do not provide a check-the-box, pass-through, or hybrid-mismatch election for a Yuhan Hoesa. A Yuhan Hoesa is mandatorily classified as a domestic corporation and taxed at entity level; non-resident ownership does not make it fiscally transparent.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Korean Value Added Tax (VAT) under the Value Added Tax Act
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No turnover exemption applies to a domestic Yuhan Hoesa: any corporate entity with a place of business in Korea must register for VAT from the moment it commences business. A foreign non-resident supplier of electronic and digital services with no Korean place of business is obliged to register for VAT under the Simplified Business Registration procedure only when its annual Korean-source taxable supplies exceed KRW 300,000,000.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All Korean VAT-registered businesses must issue e-Tax Invoices electronically through the NTS HomeTax system; the invoice must be transmitted to HomeTax by the day after the date of supply. The NTS centrally validates, stores, and reconciles the e-Tax Invoice data through the HomeTax API and dedicated portal. There is no physical fiscal stamp; the validated electronic invoice number and transmission record in HomeTax serve as the anti-fraud clearing evidence. Failure to issue or transmit e-Tax Invoices triggers denial of input VAT credits and additional tax penalties.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: The export of the manufactured frozen dim sum goods to overseas buyers qualifies for the zero rate of Korean VAT when the goods are physically exported from Korea and cleared by Korea Customs Service. The Korean LLC must hold an Export Declaration, shipping documents, and evidence that the export proceeds are received in a foreign currency via a Korean foreign exchange bank. The supply must be made to a non-resident foreign buyer and title or physical possession must pass outside Korea. Qualifying offshore digital services are zero-rated only for B2B supplies where the place of consumption is demonstrably outside Korea; B2C digital supplies to Korean consumers remain taxable at 10%.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Bill of Entry) submitted to Korea Customs Service via UNI-PASS
Original Bill of Lading (or Air Waybill for air export) issued to the Korean exporter/shipper
Certificate of Export Proceeds / Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) issued by the appointed Korean foreign exchange bank
Export sales contract or overseas purchase order and bank settlement (SWIFT LC or TT) evidence confirming payment by the foreign buyer
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: NTS, together with Korea Customs Service and the foreign exchange bank inspection authorities, may audit the export documentation trail. If an export declaration is false, goods are not physically dispatched, documents are backdated, or export proceeds are not received and reported as foreign currency export earnings within the repatriation benchmark period (180 days for the zero-rating substantiation cycle), NTS will disallow the zero rate, reassess VAT at 10% on the export consideration, impose additional taxes for unfaithful declaration or under-reporting under the Value Added Tax Act and the Framework Act on National Taxes, charge delinquency surcharges, and initiate criminal penalties under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act. Retroactive reassessment may cover five years from the statutory due date, extended to ten years in cases of fraud; suspended export VAT refunds may be clawed back with interest before any future refund is paid.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK), with delegated regulatory administration by the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea maintains a free-floating KRW with an open current account and a risk-based capital account control system administered jointly by the Bank of Korea and the Ministry of Economy and Finance under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. Current account transactions are fully convertible; export and import settlement are processed without requiring underlying prior approval, but each hard-currency receipt or payment must be tagged with a Foreign Exchange (FX) transaction code and reported to the Foreign Exchange Information Network. Capital account operations, including foreign direct investment, loans, and securities flows, are liberalized but require reporting, a receipt, or a declaration through a designated foreign exchange bank. There is no surrender obligation for exporters, but export earnings must be collected within the statutory period and deposited into foreign currency accounts. Profit remittances by the LLC to overseas shareholders are treated as outward current-account dividends: the bank requires audited financial statements, corporate tax clearance, proof of withholding dividend tax, and an FX declaration. Dividends are freely remitted once compliance is met, so no separate approval bottleneck exists for standard treasury flows.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds must be collected within 18 months from the export declaration date. There is no mandatory conversion ratio to KRW; the exporter is legally required to receive lawful foreign currency through a designated foreign exchange bank and may either retain the proceeds in a Foreign Currency Deposit Account or sell them to the bank. Any overdue collection must be justified and may require MOEF/BOK approval for extension.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Foreign Investment Capital Escrow Account and Basic Operational KRW/USD Current Account
Foreign Investment Capital Escrow Account and Basic Operational KRW/USD Current Account
Foreign Investment Capital Escrow Account and Basic Operational KRW/USD Current Account
Foreign Investment Capital Escrow Account and Basic Operational KRW/USD Current Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low feasibility as a primary treasury rail. South Korea does not grant full banking licences to offshore EMI brands, and the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act requires cross-border KRW/USD payments to pass through a domestic bank licensed to handle foreign exchange. Offshore digital EMIs such as Wise, Revolut, or Airwallex may hold multi-currency e-wallets in certain overseas markets, but they cannot issue a Korean domestic account number, connect to the Korea Financial Telecommunications & Clearings Institute (KFTC) won clearing, or lawfully act as a deposit-taking counterparty without a local bank partnership. For a Yuhan Hoesa manufacturing entity in Korea, fintech EMIs should be considered only for non-core collection-side convenience in countries where the EMI holds a valid local licence; all treasury, FX, and regulatory reporting must remain with Tier-1 designated foreign exchange banks.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a South Korean entity with non-resident shareholders, the initial account opening at Tier-1 banks requires the statutory director and the authorized signatory, or the Korean-appointed operating representative, to attend an in-branch interview in person. Remote consular proxy opening is legally possible only when the proxy holds a notarized power of attorney apostilled or consular-verified within three months, the beneficial owners provide passport and foreign residence verification, and the bank completes a video interview with the director. In practice, KB, Shinhan, Hana, and Woori will frequently escalate remote openings to head-office FIU and may insist on a physical interview before granting foreign exchange and trade settlement limits.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexplained non-resident ownership and possible nominee shareholding detected during UBO disclosure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of Incorporation, Articles of Association, full UBO registry, passports and foreign registration cards of each natural-person shareholder, complete share transfer history, signed declaration of no nominee arrangements, notarized source-of-investment letter, and bank statements from the overseas remitting account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial capital contribution appears low for an industrial frozen-food factory with no credible production-asset trail
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank-to-bank remittance record through the FIPA-designated escrow account, foreign currency purchase certificate, capital contribution verification report issued by a certified public accountant, factory lease agreement, customs-imported equipment invoices, manufacturing machinery insurance policies, and a two-year business plan with projected production capacity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Export settlement patterns show third-party payers or indirect payment of trade proceeds, a red flag for possible invoice or transfer mispricing
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Original commercial invoices, packing lists, bills of lading, Korean customs export declarations, remittance advices from the buyer's exact bank account, signed sales contracts with Incoterms definitions, and the matching Bank of Korea FX transaction declarations showing the same trade purpose code for each collection.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency dim sum exports to jurisdictions with restricted banking relationships or sanctions exposure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Comprehensive denied-party screening results against South Korean FIU, UN, OFAC, and EU lists, transport route documentation, consignee end-user certificates, container seal and cold-chain temperature logs, audited purchase orders from qualified B2B food importers, and prior import permits in destination markets.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The foreign shareholder must open a Foreign Investment Capital Escrow Account at a designated domestic bank, such as KB, Shinhan, Hana, or Woori, by presenting Foreign Investment Promotion Act registration documents. The investor remits from its own overseas corporate bank account in USD or another qualified currency using the FX purpose code for equity contribution for foreign direct investment. After the credit is received, the bank issues a Foreign Currency Purchase Certificate, the company completes legal incorporation, and the escrowed foreign currency is converted into KRW at the prevailing market rate and credited to the paid-in capital account. A certified public accountant then issues the capital contribution verification report, and the bank files the foreign investment declaration with MOEF and Bank of Korea through the Foreign Exchange Information Network.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: All trade and operating payments must be executed through the company's designated foreign exchange bank. Direct telegraphic transfers use SWIFT MT103 with the correct FX transaction purpose code and require underlying purchase contracts, pro-forma invoices, import customs declarations, and proof of manufacturing premises in Korea. For export sales, the company may collect via Commercial Letter of Credit, either sight or usance, and may use documentary collections (D/P or D/A) for consolidated invoice-based settlement. Domestic KRW payments for wages, utilities, and raw materials are cleared through KFTC rails, while any cross-border KRW distribution such as dividends or shareholder loans must be reported and settled through the designated foreign exchange bank.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable currency forwards in USD/KRW, JPY/KRW, and EUR/KRW backed by real trade exposure are permissible through designated foreign exchange banks. Non-deliverable forwards are generally restricted to specific offshore hedging structures and are not permissible as a standalone speculative product for the operating LLC. FX swaps and cross-currency interest rate swaps are permissible for balance-sheet and term-debt hedging, while FX options are allowed only with documented underlying trade exposure and full bank suitability assessments.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Business Report (Sa'eop Bogo Seo) submission for corporate income tax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of South Korea
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By March 31 of the year following the close of the fiscal year (for calendar-year taxpayers); foreign-invested companies with different fiscal years report within 15 days after the statutory corporate tax filing deadline
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file by due date triggers a 20% penalty on the unpaid corporate tax, plus daily interest of 0.022% (approximately 8% per annum) on the deficient tax amount; continued delinquency may lead to enforced tax collection and business registration cancellation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Tax Return (Beobinse) filing and payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of South Korea
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By March 31 for the immediately preceding fiscal year; if the fiscal year ends on a date other than December 31, within 3 months from the fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A 20% non-filing penalty on the tax amount; late payment penalty of 0.022% per day (about 8% per annum) accrues on the unpaid amount; chronic non-compliance can trigger seizure of assets and criminal referral for tax evasion.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local Income Tax Return (Jibang Sodeukse) for the municipal surtax on corporate tax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local government (Si/Gun/Gu) tax authority where the registered office is located
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 10 days after the corporate tax filing deadline, i.e., by April 10 for calendar-year companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing penalty of 20% of the local income tax amount; daily late-payment surcharge of 0.022% applies; continued delinquency may lead to local administrative collection procedures and business registration restrictions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements filing and publication (for external users) if entity meets disclosure thresholds
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) / DART system (for statutory external audit targets); National Tax Service (NTS) for attached financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the fiscal year-end (standard annual shareholder meeting deadline); DART filing within 90 days from fiscal year-end for listed or public-interest entities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file audited statements for an externally audited entity is subject to penalties under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies (up to KRW 20 million in fines); administrative measures may include notification of audit failure to the FSS and referral to the Securities & Futures Commission.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Withholding and VAT annual reconciliation filings
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of South Korea
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Semi-annual VAT returns due January 25 and July 25; annual withholding summary due March 10 for the prior calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late VAT filing penalty up to 10% of unpaid tax for first violation, escalating to 20%; withholding reporting penalties up to 5% for failure to report wage/interest income; repeated violations may trigger intensive tax investigations and business closure orders.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Workplace-level annual Labor & Welfare filings (health insurance, national pension, employment insurance) and minimum wage compliance statement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Pension Service, National Health Insurance Service, Korea Employment & Labor Officials (Ministry of Employment and Labor)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Employment insurance and industrial accident insurance annual variable rate declarations due by March 15 (for prior year); health insurance and pension contribution filings are continuous, with annual end-of-year reporting through March 31
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late declaration penalties up to 5% of unpaid contributions; employer criminal liability for failing to withhold statutory social insurance contributions; registration of delinquency with the Korean credit information system and forced collection of contributions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Business License (Sa'eopja Deungrokjeung) renewal confirmation / continuous maintenance confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) South Korea (local tax office)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No fixed annual renewal date; continuous obligation to maintain updated business registration; annual compliance confirmation occurs through the regular tax return process; any change of address/business item must be reported within 15 days
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to report changes may result in a KRW 2,000,000 penalty under the Framework Act on National Taxes; operating without valid business registration after closure can trigger administrative cancellation and tax collection against the representative personally.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual franchise/restaurant registration renewal (if on-site factory sells direct to consumer/premises)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Food and Drug Safety (MFDS) / local district office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Renewal every 2 years for food manufacturing establishments; reporting of any modification in manufacturing line within 15 days
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal imposes administrative fines up to KRW 3,000,000 and immediate suspension of operations; operation without valid permit is subject to criminal prosecution under the Food Sanitation Act, including imprisonment up to 1 year or fines up to KRW 10,000,000.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies (amended, effective for fiscal years starting on/after January 1, 2019): external audit is mandatory if an entity meets ANY of the following at fiscal year-end: (a) total assets exceed KRW 12 billion (~USD 9,200,000); (b) total revenue exceeds KRW 10 billion (~USD 7,700,000); (c) number of employees exceeds 500; (d) total shareholders' equity exceeds KRW 12 billion for non-listed companies, or KRW 5 billion for listed/public-listed entities; also the Financial Supervisory Service may designate an entity as 'public-interest' based on industry, size, and market impact. For small- or medium-sized Yuhan Hoesa without mandatory external audit, a compiled or reviewed financial statement may be prepared for tax purposes, but if loans from Korean financial institutions exceed KRW 500 million, banks typically require audited statements under the Korean external audit thresholds for credit risk assessment.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) for entities subject to mandatory external audit; 'General Corporate Accounting Standards' (기업회계기준, K-GAAP) or 'SME Accounting Standards' (중소기업회계기준) for non-mandatory-audit private companies; all tax financial statements filed with NTS must reconcile to the statutory tax base under the Corporate Income Tax Act, and the FSS accepts K-IFRS for publicly accountable entities.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the Korean Commercial Act and the Act on Real Name Financial Transactions and Confidentiality, a Yuhan Hoesa is required to maintain a current register of members/shareholders, but South Korea does not impose a separate annual UBO confirmation filing for private limited companies generally; any change in members or shareholders must be filed with the court registry within 30 days of the change where the alteration affects the registered capital or ownership percentage; moreover, for foreign-owned entities, the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) requires foreign investment report within 30 days for share transfers or changes in foreign ownership ratios under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act; the NTS Beneficial Ownership Rule (effective under tax treaties and OECD BEPS implementation) demands annual reporting of substantial controlling shareholders in the corporate tax return when a foreign entity controls a Korean company; all ownership movements must be documented and made accessible to the tax authority upon request.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Charges/Mortgages (if any security interests exist)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 500 to USD 1,200 per year for standard registered office/agent services in Seoul or Gyeonggi province
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,500 to USD 9,000 per year for a certified independent audit for a medium-sized frozen food manufacturing entity under K-IFRS

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% top marginal rate on a progressive scale: 9% on income up to KRW 200M; 19% above KRW 200M to KRW 20B; 21% above KRW 20B to KRW 300B; 24% above KRW 300B.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Qualifying foreign-invested enterprises in free economic zones and special industrial zones may access a 100% corporate income tax holiday for up to 5 years and a 50% reduction for the following 3 years; additional incentives include R&D tax credits, SME tax exemptions, and a preferential patent or intellectual-property income regime for qualifying patented manufacturing technology.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: South Korean Corporate Income Tax Return and Taxable Income Calculation Schedule filed under Article 60 of the Corporate Income Tax Act through the National Tax Service HomeTax electronic filing portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: By the last day of the third month after the fiscal year-end; for a December 31 year-end the return is due by March 31, extended to the next business day if the due date falls on a weekend or public holiday.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box A-1: Domestic/Foreign Corporation Status, Head Office, and Place of Effective Management
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of the entity legal seat, head office address, management location, and classification as a resident or non-resident corporation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Yuhan Hoesa is a Korean-resident domestic corporation because it is incorporated in Korea, so it is taxable on worldwide income. Non-resident foreign shareholders are not taxed at the entity level on the CIT return unless they have a Korean permanent establishment. If a foreign director's authority and physical presence in Korea create a fixed place of business, the return must declare that fact to prevent an unintended permanent establishment exposure.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box B-10: Gross Revenue from Manufacturing and Sales
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross sales of prefabricated quick-frozen dim sum and dumplings, including domestic and export invoices settled through SWIFT letters of credit and TT wire transfers.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All export revenue must be reported in KRW using the Bank of Korea base exchange rate on the invoice or settlement date. Intercompany exports to overseas related distributors must be recorded at the arm's-length price, and any transfer-pricing adjustment under the International Tax Adjustment Act must be added to or deducted from the declared gross income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box C-15: Deductible Expenses and Related-Party Recharges
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating expenses for raw materials, cold-chain labor, production equipment, quality control, freight, intercompany management fees, royalties, and interest.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payments to non-resident related parties are deductible only when supported by written contracts, actual benefit evidence, and arm's-length charges. Royalties and interest remitted abroad require withholding of 22% aggregate tax unless a DTA applies; if the withholding is not performed, the expense may be disallowed and the withholding agent faces collection and penalty liability.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box D-20: Taxable Base, Loss Carryforwards, and Foreign Tax Credit
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of taxable income after statutory book-tax reconciliation, claimed loss carryforwards, foreign-source income inclusions, and foreign tax credit offset.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign-source income attributable to the Korean factory must be included on the Korean return. A foreign tax credit is limited to the Korean corporate income tax attributable to the same foreign-source income. Loss carryforwards may be claimed for five years only and are not available to an entity that lacks real operational substance or that has been restructured to traffic in tax losses.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box E-30: Non-Resident Distributions and Withholding Tax Summary
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of dividends, interest, royalties, and other income paid or credited to non-resident shareholders, lenders, or licensors, together with the resulting final withholding taxes.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For an outbound dividend to a non-resident shareholder of Yuhan Hoesa, withhold 22% aggregate (20% national tax plus 2% local income tax surcharge) unless a bilateral tax treaty grants a reduced rate. To apply the DTA rate, attach the non-resident recipient's Tax Residency Certificate, beneficial ownership statement, and the National Tax Service application for tax exemption or reduction before remittance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box F-40: Tax Incentives, Investment Subsidies, and Alternative Minimum Tax Adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Schedule for claiming R&D credits, foreign-investment tax holidays, free-zone preferential rates, intellectual property income deductions, and any alternative minimum tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Incentives are available only if the Korean entity performs actual production, employment, investment, and management functions in Korea. Passive non-resident shareholders cannot aggregate their positions to claim free-zone or R&D incentives where the business is a pure shell; such claims must be recaptured with penalties if substance is found lacking.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file by the statutory deadline triggers an unfiled-return penalty of up to 20% of the unpaid tax, or a fixed KRW 200,000 penalty when no tax is due; omission or understatement of taxable income triggers penalties of 40% to 60% under the National Tax Basic Act; late payment accrues a daily surcharge of 0.022%; fraudulent filing is prosecuted under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act with imprisonment of up to 5 years and fines of up to three times the evaded tax.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% aggregate withholding tax on outbound dividends: 20% national withholding under Article 98 of the Corporate Income Tax Act plus 2% local income tax surcharge, subject to reduction under an applicable double tax treaty for a qualifying beneficial owner.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim DTA relief, the non-resident recipient must submit the National Tax Service application for non-resident income tax exemption or reduction before payment, provide a Tax Residency Certificate issued by its home tax authority, prove beneficial ownership and absence of treaty shopping, and maintain source documents for the dividend distribution. If tax was over-withheld, the recipient may file a refund application with the district tax office attaching the Tax Residency Certificate, withholding certificate, and beneficial ownership declaration within the statutory refund limitation period. Korea will deny treaty relief where the recipient is a pure conduit or shell corporation.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: The statutory withholding rate on outbound royalties and interest is 22% aggregate (20% national plus 2% local surcharge). Treaty rates vary by counterparty; most Korean DTA protocols reduce interest to 10% to 15% and royalties to 10% to 15% for the beneficial owner, with full exemption in limited intercompany or public-institution scenarios.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: KRW 10 billion in cross-border related-party transactions for Local File preparation, with a KRW 100 billion multinational group consolidated revenue threshold for Master File preparation; a related-party transaction disclosure schedule is separately required for cross-border transactions exceeding KRW 5 billion per counterparty or KRW 1 billion in aggregate.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: South Korea does not operate UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations, but it applies an equivalent substance-over-form doctrine through the place-of-effective-management test in Article 6 of the Corporate Income Tax Act, the controlled-foreign-company rules in the International Tax Adjustment Act, and the general anti-abuse principles of the National Tax Basic Act. For the prefabricated dim sum factory, the Korean entity must retain Core Income-Generating Activities including production, quick-freezing, cold-chain storage, raw material procurement, invoicing, and product risk; if those activities are shifted to a low-tax related party while only minimal assets are left in Korea, the Korean tax authority will reattribute the profit to Yuhan Hoesa and impose penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate omission of export revenue received through SWIFT LC and TT wire rails, issuance of fabricated purchase invoices for raw materials, and filing of an inflated loss position to reduce or eliminate the Korean corporate income tax liability of Yuhan Hoesa.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 3 of the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act imposes imprisonment of up to 5 years or a fine of up to three times the tax evaded; the National Tax Basic Act and Corporate Income Tax Act impose additional understatement penalties of up to 60% plus daily late-payment surcharges on the corrected tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Korean courts pierce the corporate veil where the entity is a mere instrument of fraud; the responsible director is jointly and severally liable for the corporate tax debt from personal assets, may be blacklisted and subject to a departure ban by the National Tax Service, and faces criminal imprisonment, asset seizure, and disqualification as a director.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing / Shell Company Substance Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Selling prefabricated dim sum and dumplings to an offshore affiliate at below-cost prices, attributing the residual manufacturing margin to a low-substance intermediary, and failing to prepare and submit the required Local File and Master File documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 7 of the International Tax Adjustment Act permits the Korean tax authority to compute the arm's-length price and adjust taxable income; Article 13 imposes additional tax of up to 30% of the adjusted related-party transaction income and a KRW 100 million penalty for material failure to file transfer pricing documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who certify false intercompany pricing or substance reports can be held personally liable for the resulting corporate tax deficiencies under the abuse-of-rights doctrine and joint liability principles; egregious cases carry criminal tax evasion liability, personal asset restitution, travel blacklisting, and imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using layered nominee bank accounts or shell intermediaries to receive SWIFT LC proceeds for frozen-food exports without filing the required foreign exchange transaction reports, beneficially owning or controlling the underlying receipts, or reporting unusual transactions under the Financial Transaction Reports Act.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Financial Transaction Reports Act and Foreign Exchange Transactions Act impose fines up to KRW 100 million and imprisonment of up to 3 years for undisclosed or unlicensed foreign exchange transactions and deliberate AML reporting omissions; the National Tax Service may also disallow deductions for undocumented foreign payments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The representative director and AML compliance director face personal criminal liability for failure to detect or report unusual transactions; personal assets traceable to undeclared export proceeds may be confiscated, a travel ban may be imposed pending criminal proceedings, and imprisonment of up to 3 years may be imposed in a criminal conviction.
